newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Tsy's Rubin says budget talks "constructive".
newsitem.headline: U.S. Tsy's Rubin says budget talks "constructive".

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin described a meeting with members of Congress on taxes as "constructive," but said no decisions resulted from the meeting.
Rubin said the meeting was a "useful, constructive, exchange of views." The meeting was part of budget talks taking place between congressional budget leaders and White House officials this week.
House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, a Texas Republican, said the meeting was preliminary and was intended only to get the positions of all sides on the table.
"These are preliminary, there's no resolution to anything at a meeting like this at this time," Archer told reporters.
He said no new tax proposals were put on the table at the meeting.
On the capital gains tax, Archer said, "we're apart, but I think we'll ultimately resolve the capital gains issue."
House Speaker Newt Gingrich, a Georgia Republican, said Wednesday he favored abolishing the capital gains tax.

Asked how far apart the various sides were on the dollar amount of tax proposals, Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican, replied: "We've never reached even an understanding on dollars, but various major players in this equation describe what they think the dollars should be, but we haven't arrived at any, we haven't finished the budget yet."
